title: The Last Escarpment
premise: Lena Delacroix, a desert ranger who has spent two decades erasing himself into the escarpment country after a wrongful conviction he never served time for, is hired to find a vanished government survey team. The trail leads him to a hidden valley community of fugitives and forgotten people who have built a life outside the law, and to the thief he was chasing: a young woman carrying evidence that the survey team was erased deliberately to bury a water-rights scandal. As the first snows close the high passes, Lena must choose between delivering the truth to courts that once condemned him and protecting the valley that offers him the belonging he never believed he deserved. He chooses both, smuggling the evidence out through the storm while staying behind to defend the valley, and in the epilogue-tinged final chapters, justice arrives not as a verdict but as the valley's survival and his own decision to finally be found.
about_author: Mirabel Okonkwo is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six years mapping arid rangelands before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember what people try to forget.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Establishes his solitary patrol routine on the escarpment, his habit of measuring life in distance, and his careful anonymity. A telegram arrives: a survey team has vanished. Emotional beat: the unease of being needed after years of choosing invisibility.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the dusty town of Harrow Bend, officials offer him the search contract, paying too well for a routine job. He notices their nervousness about the team's final survey quadrant. Beat: suspicion planted; he takes the job for reasons he won't name.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Lena's POV at the abandonment site. Tents intact, instruments packed, food untouched—yet no footprints leaving camp. His tracker's logic fails for the first time in twenty years. Beat: professional pride curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Thief on the Flats
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. He picks up a single set of tracks heading toward the forbidden high range and realizes they match the thief he's been quietly tracking all season. Beat: two mysteries braiding into one; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: What the Rocks Keep
chapters.summary: Interlude from the thief's POV, unnamed. She moves through slot canyons with a satchel she guards like a child, remembering the survey camp and why she ran. Beat: sympathy established; her fear is of people, not the desert.

chapters.title: Water Sign
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At a seep only locals know, he finds fresh sign and a torn map fragment showing a quadrant marked with government red ink. Someone surveyed land no one was supposed to know held water. Beat: the stakes widen from missing men to buried secrets.

chapters.title: Harrow Bend Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV back in town. An old rancher who once testified against him hints that the survey team asked about the escarpment's hidden valley—and about Lena himself. Beat: his past surfaces; paranoia sharpens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Pass Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weather turning early, he commits to crossing the high range now or losing the trail until spring. He sends his horse back and goes light. Beat: point of no return; exhilaration under the fear.

chapters.title: Snares and Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The thief sets defensive snares, sensing pursuit; Lena reads them and recognizes skilled, desperate hands—not a criminal's work but a survivor's. Beat: hunter begins to see prey as a person.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Snow catches him above the tree line; he shelters in a cave and finds old smoke stains—someone winters here regularly. Beat: vulnerability; the mountain strips his competence down to endurance.

chapters.title: The Valley Below
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Descending through fog, he sees it: terraced gardens, stone houses, smoke—a settlement that appears on no map. Beat: wonder and alarm; everything invisible is suddenly visible.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Thief's POV (named now as Sera). Valley scouts capture Lena; she argues against killing him, recognizing the ranger whose reputation for fairness outlaws still trade stories about. Beat: mercy as a contested choice.

chapters.title: People Without Papers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV among the valley folk: deserters, debt-fugitives, families fleeing seizures. Their elder, Amara, explains the valley survives because the government believes it's worthless—until the survey. Beat: belonging offered where he least expects it.

chapters.title: The Survey Team's Fate
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. She reveals the surveyors came armed with eviction orders; a confrontation in a storm killed three, and the rest fled rather than report a valley they'd been paid to erase. Beat: moral complexity—the vanished are neither innocent nor villains.

chapters.title: Sera's Satchel
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She was the survey team's junior clerk who discovered the quadrant reports were falsified to hide the aquifer and justify a land grab; she stole the originals and ran. Beat: the thief becomes the witness.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, confiding in Amara by the fire. He tells the story of his conviction—a rigged negligence charge after a reservoir failure that killed nine, engineered by the same water interests. Beat: his exile reframed as another buried injustice.

chapters.title: The Same Hand
chapters.summary: Lena and Sera compare documents and memories: the company behind his conviction funds the new survey. The past and present are one conspiracy. Beat: private grievance becomes shared cause; reluctant alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Voices for Staying
chapters.summary: Valley council debate, multiple short POVs. Some want to send Sera's evidence out and risk exposure; others want to burn it and stay hidden forever. Lena, the outsider, is asked to vote. Beat: he belongs enough to be argued over.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. He votes to take the evidence out himself before the passes seal—arguing a valley that hides forever has already lost. The council agrees, barely. Beat: leadership assumed; dread of the crossing.

chapters.title: Preparing the Crossing
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She teaches Lena the documents' structure and codes while the valley provisions him: dried food, a copy of the papers sewn into his coat, the originals cached. Beat: trust made tangible in stitches and salted meat.

chapters.title: The Scout Who Left
chapters.summary: A valley scout named Doss defects, stealing a horse and knowledge of the cache location, hoping to sell the valley out for amnesty. Beat: betrayal; the plan's clock starts ticking violently.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Lena's POV racing Doss across the high flats, using twenty years of route-craft to cut corners no map shows. Beat: the hunter fully returned—but now hunting for others, not himself.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Climactic chase in a flood-carved narrows. Doss's horse falls; Lena saves Doss from the water, and Doss, shamed, confesses who sent him: the company's man in Harrow Bend. Beat: mercy repaid with truth.

chapters.title: What Doss Knows
chapters.summary: Lena and Doss sheltering together. Doss reveals a company posse is already assembling to enter the valley before spring—and that the missing survey survivors are being hunted too. Beat: the deadline moves closer; the valley can't just hide.

chapters.title: Turning Back
chapters.summary: Lena's POV at the pass mouth as blizzard walls rise. With the passes closing behind him, he cannot reach the courts in time and cannot abandon the valley. He turns around. Beat: sacrifice of the mission for the people; identity shifting.

chapters.title: Homecoming in White
chapters.summary: Valley POV chorus. Lena stumbles back into the valley half-frozen; Sera and Amara nurse him. The community debates war preparations while he sleeps. Beat: he is cared for—belonging made physical.

chapters.title: Fortifying the Escarpment
chapters.summary: Lena's POV leading defense planning, using ranger knowledge to design false trails, rockfall traps, and decoy fires. Beat: his exile skills become gifts; purpose replaces hiding.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She proposes a second plan: she'll carry copies out alone through a southern route she scouted as a clerk, splitting the risk. Beat: courage passed between them; unspoken affection acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Company Men Arrive
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The posse enters the range early, led by a cold company fixer named Verrin, following Doss's partial knowledge. First skirmish at the false trails. Beat: open conflict begins; the valley's invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Traps in the Snow
chapters.summary: Lena's POV directing the defense. Rockfalls and misdirection bleed the posse's morale without killing—Lena insists on driving them out, not slaughtering them. Beat: justice outside the law defined as restraint.

chapters.title: Verrin's Offer
chapters.summary: Verrin, captured briefly then released under a flag, offers Lena full pardon and reinstatement if he surrenders the documents and the valley's leaders. Beat: temptation aimed exactly at his oldest wound.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Lena's POV answering Verrin at the valley gate: he names the nine dead from the reservoir collapse aloud, one by one, and refuses. Beat: the novel's thematic climax of character; his past laid down.

chapters.title: Sera Through the South Route
chapters.summary: Sera's POV on her solo crossing—avalanche terrain, a frozen river, near-death, and the discovery that Verrin split his force and a rider shadows her. Beat: terror and resolve; the second front opens.

chapters.title: The Shadow Rider
chapters.summary: Sera's POV confronting her pursuer: one of the surviving surveyors, not hunting her but fleeing Verrin, willing to testify. Beat: an enemy becomes an ally; the evidence gains a living witness.

chapters.title: Storm at the Gate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Verrin, humiliated and exposed by weather, makes a final assault up the main draw during the season's worst storm. The valley holds using every trap laid. Beat: military climax; chaos, loss, courage.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: Aftermath, multiple POVs. The valley buries two defenders; Amara is wounded. Verrin retreats with his force broken, promising legal ruin instead. Beat: grief inside victory; the price of standing visible.

chapters.title: Out of the Mountains
chapters.summary: Sera's POV reaching Harrow Bend and, through a journalist ally of Lena's old acquaintance, delivering documents and testimony to federal investigators arriving ahead of the thaw. Beat: the law finally reached from outside it.

chapters.title: Verdicts and Water
chapters.summary: Spring, multiple POVs. Indictments fall on the company; the aquifer is protected; surviving surveyors testify; Lena's conviction is formally vacated. Beat: justice rendered without erasing the valley's autonomy.

chapters.title: The Map That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Officials offer him a commission to map the region; he submits a map that leaves the valley blank, and they accept, believing nothing is there. Beat: quiet triumph; protection through chosen invisibility.

chapters.title: Staying Found
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, final chapter. He unpacks the belongings he kept ready to flee for twenty years and hangs them on real hooks. Sera plants a garden row beside his. Beat: resolution—belonging chosen, memory honored, home measured in years at last.
